about: The priest asks God to make the offering blessed, duly recognized, ratified, spiritual and acceptable. The final petition asks that it may become for us the Body and Blood of God’s dearly beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

seg.tr: O God, we ask You graciously to make this offering in all respects

ex.w003: The expressed subject pronoun, which Latin usually omits, emphasizes the addressee named immediately as “Deus” (w004).

seg.nr: The priest makes three signs of the cross over the offerings.

seg.tr: blessed, approved, ratified, spiritual, and acceptable,

ex.w011: The Latin adjective is related to “reason” and can also be translated “reasonable” or “rational.” Here it describes the offering in the language of spiritual worship. The following petition asks that it become for us Christ’s Body and Blood.

seg.nr: The priest makes one sign of the cross over the Host alone, at the word Corpus.

seg.tr: so that for us it may become the Body

ex.w017: The understood subject is the “oblátio” introduced at the beginning of the prayer, so the verb is singular.

seg.nr: The priest makes one sign of the cross over the chalice alone, at the word Sanguis.

seg.tr: and Blood of Your dearly beloved Son,
